title: Mechanistic Interpretability Needs Philosophy
claim: A field's open problems each decompose into foundational conceptual questions that a partner discipline can help clarify.
layout: Title banner above 3 stacked rows, each with a right-side icon
description: A wide, short, text-based figure with no plots or data. A gold-gradient banner at the top holds the italic bold title 'How Philosophy Can Help Clarify Mechanistic Interpretability' and a subtitle saying three open problems in MI and the philosophical questions behind them. Below it are three horizontally stacked rows separated by thin lines, with the middle row shaded light gray. Each row has a bold numbered heading that states an open problem: decomposing networks, what 'features' AI systems discover, and detecting deception from model internals. Under each heading, a few sentences of philosophical sub-questions, such as 'What is decomposition?' and 'What is deception, what is lying?'. A small black line icon sits at the right edge of each row: a tree diagram, a magnifying glass over a box, and a horse with a warning sign. The eye goes first to the gold title banner, then down the rows.
caption: How philosophy can help: a case based on three open problems in MI.
abstract: Mechanistic interpretability (MI) aims to explain how trained neural networks work by uncovering their underlying mechanisms. As the field grows in influence, it is increasingly important to examine not just models themselves, but the assumptions, concepts and explanatory strategies implicit in MI research. We argue that mechanistic interpretability needs philosophy as an ongoing partner in clarifying its concepts, refining its methods, and navigating the epistemic and ethical complexities of interpreting AI systems. There is significant unrealised potential for progress in MI to be gained through deeper engagement with philosophers and philosophical frameworks. Taking three open problems from the MI literature as examples, this paper illustrates the value philosophy can add to MI research, and outlines a path toward deeper interdisciplinary dialogue.
